statements.quote:
Informed consent was obtained from both students and their legal guardians, 
ensuring voluntary participation and confidentiality of data.
statements.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 20), Methodology, ethics paragraph; data-confidentiality statement.

statements.quote:
The Generative AI 
integrated lesson plans were meticulously structured, comprising five distinct teaching stages: 
1) Warm-up stage, 2) Presentation stage, 3) Practice stage, 4) Production stage, and 5) Wrap-
up stage (refer to Figure 1 for a detailed outline).
statements.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 21), Research Instruments, item 1; internal pointer to lesson-plan outline in Figure 1 on PDF p. 6.

statements.quote:
The lesson plans mirrored those of the 
Generative AI integrated approach, featuring five teaching stages:  1)  Warm- up stage, 2) 
Presentation stage, 3) Practice stage, 4) Production stage, and 5) Wrap-up stage (Figure 2).
statements.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 22), Research Instruments, item 2; internal pointer to lesson-plan outline in Figure 2 on PDF p. 7.

statements.quote:
Each student was tasked with selecting a writing prompt provided by the researcher, tasked 
with crafting a narrative within a specified time limit of 50 minutes.
statements.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 23), Research Instruments, item 3, Creative Writing Skills Assessment; researcher-provided prompts.

statements.quote:
They employed the 5-point scoring rubric, which covered five distinct dimensions: 
1) Creativity, 2) Development, 3) Voice, 4) Literary Devices, and 5) Literary Conventions (refer 
to Table 1 for detailed criteria).
statements.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 23), Research Instruments, item 3; internal pointer to scoring rubric in Table 1 on PDF pp. 8-9.

statements.quote:
Examples of writing prompts included: (1) Compose a short story 
inspired by the image of an abandoned house in the woods; (2) Imagine you are stranded on 
a deserted island; (3) Write a journal entry detailing your experiences and emotions; (4) Create 
a dialogue between two characters who find themselves in a mysterious situation.
statements.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 24), Research Instruments, continuation of item 3; example task materials.

statements.quote:
The resulting narratives 
varied in length, typically ranging from 300 to 500 words, allowing students to explore their 
ideas and develop their storytelling abilities within the given constraints.
statements.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 24), Research Instruments, continuation of item 3; description of participant narratives, without a release or access statement.

statements.quote:
These pretest scores 
served as the baseline data for this initial stage.
statements.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 25), Data Collection, item 2, Pre-Learning Assessment; baseline-data description.

statements.quote:
The data 
collected at this stage constituted the participants' posttest scores, providing insights into the 
impact of the teaching interventions on their creative writing skills.
statements.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 26), Data Collection, item 4, Post-Learning Assessment; posttest-data description.

notes:
Checked on 2026-10-09. Read the complete 411-line markdown conversion in sequential chunks, including all references, and checked the relevant PDF passages with PyMuPDF. The saved article is the 18-page journal version, printed pp. 17-34; the publisher's current PDF matches it exactly. No appendix, acknowledgment containing an availability statement, supplementary-file notice, preregistration, repository link, data/code release statement, or offer of data on request was found. The only embedded PDF link is the corresponding author's mailto link, which was not contacted. forms/c421.json has empty data_url and code_url values.

The statements array preserves the paper's data-confidentiality sentence, descriptions and internal pointers for study materials, descriptions identifying the generated narratives/scores, and the sole external document citation. These are not statements that participant data have been released. Lesson outlines appear in Figures 1-2, prompt examples in Research Instruments, and the scoring rubric in Table 1. Quotations are copied from PDF text with its extracted line breaks retained. Published Tables 2-4 contain aggregate results, not participant records. The article and its in-text materials are not counted as a separate data deposit.

All four requested repository APIs were searched by full title, a shorter distinctive title phrase, and first-author surname. Successful searches returned no deposit for this study. Full-title queries used the ASCII-apostrophe title from candidates.json; the shorter title searches avoid that punctuation difference. DataCite's two author-name hits and Zenodo's one author-name hit were unrelated works; their exclusions are documented in searches. Both initial Zenodo requests returned HTTP 400 for size=100, and both were rerun successfully at the unauthenticated limit of 25. No account, authentication, access request, or bypass was attempted. OSF checks cover public node titles and do not establish whether a private project or a project under another title exists. Confidence is high in the documented none-found outcome within these sources, not proof that no unindexed or private data exist.

The sole HTTP URL in the PDF/markdown is http://academic.obec.go.th/images/document/1525235513_d_1.pdf in References, PDF p. 17 (printed p. 33), for the Ministry of Education's Basic Education Core Curriculum 2008 (Revised 2017). The original HTTP request had no HTTP response: http_status=null, URLError/WinError 10061 (connection actively refused). The HTTPS version, https://academic.obec.go.th/images/document/1525235513_d_1.pdf, returned HTTP 403 Forbidden; inspection stopped. This is a background curriculum citation, not a study-data deposit. The publisher landing page and PDF viewer/download returned HTTP 200. The landing page displays a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International license for the article; no dataset license was found.

No relevant deposit or participant/output data file was located, so there are no confirmed rows, columns, participant identifiers, arm labels, outcome scores, or participant texts to inspect. Public data therefore cannot currently resolve S1 posttest analyzed N by arm, complete-pair N, or the printed-test-statistic validity questions in final.open_items; nor can they supply unreported component means, standard deviations, standard errors, or diversity measures from narratives. Rater procedures and randomization details also remain unconfirmed. Nothing was inferred about data access from the confidentiality statement. No files were downloaded to disk, and the only file written was forms/data/c421.json.
